assessments.reasoning: This fresh SCES-1.0 execution reacquired the claim, publisher plaintext, SPDX plaintext, and official release tag. The official tag identifies commit 04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3 and lists COPYING.RUNTIME in its tree. The pinned publisher fetch uses that same commit and path. The fixed-source tool reported 1,284 bytes for the public revision 1 claim and a SHA-256 matching the requested record digest. The claim's provenance field matches the reported publisher SHA-256, 9d6b43ce4d8de0c878bf16b54d8e7a10d9bd42b75178153e3af6a815bdc90f74. The decoded bodies matched the reported lengths and returned source text. The conclusion rests on the publisher notice, with SPDX used for the byte-identity challenge. [Official GCC release tag](https://gnu.googlesource.com/gcc/+/refs/tags/releases/gcc-14.2.0) [Pinned publisher plaintext](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3/COPYING.RUNTIME) [Public claim record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/software-commons/license-index/07d2dc0940278ca642b5f758a48c99605415b0c9/sces/records/claim/gcc-14-2-runtime-exception-31-document-redistribution--1.json)

challenge.method: Compared the decoded publisher and SPDX bodies directly, then removed SPDX's added General information line and normalized whitespace to check whether the remaining wording matched. Tested a full publisher copy with the LF at zero-based byte offset 196 replaced by one ASCII space. Read §1 against the opening notice to test whether its software conditions applied to document copying.
challenge.results: The 3,324-byte publisher file and the 3,390-byte SPDX file differ. SPDX's reported SHA-256 is 7103d4f7f7e2f8ce10d282a05e0689637f8d6d9ef7b399d808d1da313e69b960. The first differing byte is at offset 59, where SPDX inserts its General information line before the copyright line. SPDX also reflows the text, including the opening notice. After removing the added line and normalizing whitespace, the wording matches. The single LF-to-space substitution preserves the words and file length but defeats exact-byte identity. Both the substituted copy and the fetched SPDX representation are outside the claim's exact-byte scope. Section 1 supplies no conflicting condition for verbatim document copying. [Pinned SPDX plaintext](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/license-list-data/31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48/text/GCC-exception-3.1.txt)

limitations: The assessment covers verbatim copies of the cited GCC 14.2.0 plaintext. Software permissions for particular works, modified copies, trademark rights, canonical identity, and SPDX correspondence remain outside the claim.
The byte comparison leaves any independent legal basis for SPDX publication unresolved.
reasoning: The publisher's half-open byte range [59,247) contains the FSF copyright line and the complete opening notice. Its reported SHA-256 is 9a4b2500a51e7d2e1e736614195c9d5e53b3bec7e8fd580391951d03f5f06c09. The notice says “Everyone is permitted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this license document” and expressly bars changing it. This matches the actor, action, object, and verbatim-copy condition in the revision 1 claim. Section 1 separately permits propagation of Target Code that combines the Runtime Library with Independent Modules when all Target Code was generated by Eligible Compilation Processes. It permits conveying that combination under terms consistent with the Independent Modules' licensing. Those conditions govern the software grant. The opening notice supplies the document-copy permission. [Pinned publisher plaintext](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3/COPYING.RUNTIME)
